header.running_head: The Da'wah that The Sahabah (RA) Gave to Various Tribes and Arabs

blocks.text: those from his people who had accepted Islaam. At the time Rasulullaah ﷺ was in Khaybar. Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) eventually reached Madinah with seventy or eighty families from the Dows tribe.[^1]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) has also narrated from Hadhrat Tufayl bin Amr (RA) the story of how he accepted Islaam, how he gave Da'wah to his father, his wife and his people and his arrival in Makkah, just as it was mentioned in the previous narration. However, the narration of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) adds that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) to burn an idol called Dhul Kaffayn. In addition, it also mentions that Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) thereafter left for Yamaamah where he saw a dream and was then martyred in the Battle of Yamaamah.[^2]

Another narration states that when Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) arrived in Makkah, some people from the Quraysh told him about Rasulullaah ﷺ and requested him to assess Rasulullaah ﷺ. He therefore went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and recited some of his poetry to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ then recited Surah Ikhlaas and the Mu'awwadhatayn (Surahs Falaq and Naas) to him. He accepted Islaam on the spot and then returned to his people. The narration then goes on to speak about his whip and its light. The narrator mentions further that Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) then invited his parents to Islaam. His father accepted Islaam but his mother did not. When he invited his tribesmen, it was only Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) who accepted.

Thereafter, Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, "Would you like a fortified stronghold with strong defences?" he was referring to the territory of the Dows tribe (which he wanted Rasulullaah ﷺ to take hold of after cursing the Dows tribe). However, when Rasulullaah ﷺ made du'aa for the Dows tribe instead, Hadhrat Tufayl (RA) said, "This is not what I wanted." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "There are many of them who are just like you."

Amongst the Dows tribe was a person called Jundub bin Amr bin Humama bin Auf who used to say during the Period of Ignorance, "I know that the Creation has a Creator but I do not know who it is." When he heard of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he went to Rasulullaah ﷺ along with seventy five men of his tribe and they all accepted Islaam. Hadhrat Abu Hurayra (RA) narrates that Jundub placed each man individually before Rasulullaah ﷺ.

(Apart from the above,) Many narrations have already passed (that are also relevant to this discussion) such as the narrations mentioning the Da'wah Hadhrat Ali (RA) gave to the Hamdaan tribe[^3], the Da'wah Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) gave to the Banu Haarith bin Ka'b[^4] tribe and the Da'wah Hadhrat Abu Umaama (RA) gave to his tribe[^5]
Abu Nu'aym in Dalaa'il (Pg.78) as quoted in Al Bidaaya wan Nihaaya (Vol.3 Pg.100). Commentary on the chain of narrators is mentioned in Isaaba (Vol.2 Pg.225). Ibn Sa'd has also narrated the Hadith.
